summary: @servicetitan/startup ships obfuscated preinstall that downloads Bun and executes a 728KB opaque payload
details: The package's `preinstall` script runs `node setup.mjs`, an obfuscated helper using hex-mangled identifiers (`_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e`) and string-property indirection (`_0x19328d.YCZJE(execFileSync,...)`). At install time it downloads the Bun runtime binary from `github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<platform>.zip`, unzips it, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js` — a ~728KB single-line JavaScript blob using a rotated string-array cipher (`WV8StW`/`hc1jfK9`, 3000+ entry table, no readable strings). Executing the payload under a freshly fetched alternate runtime prevents Node-based inspection of what actually runs. The package presents itself as a Lerna/TypeScript/React scaffolder; nothing about that stated purpose requires downloading a second language runtime, and the README does not document this behavior. The obfuscation style of `setup.mjs` and `math_init.js` is also inconsistent with the package's other source files (e.g. `src/postinstall.js`, which is clean and commented), consistent with an implanted install-time payload rather than a legitimate build step.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
